issues.legal_issue: A tenant who pays the initial arrears on time and thereafter pays rent with reasonable punctuality is not liable to eviction merely because some payments are not mathematically punctual.
material_facts: The amount of standard rent was disputed, so the provision governing cases other than those with no dispute about standard rent applied.
The tenant deposited all arrears at the interim rent fixed by the court within the time directed.

Thereafter, rent was deposited for periods of two or three months at a time; some deposits were delayed by a few days, with the longest delay being 23 days, but rent for most months was deposited in advance.
The trial court had required monthly rent to be deposited by the fifth day of each succeeding month.
The lower courts ordered eviction for default in payment of rent, treating the deposits as insufficiently regular.
issues.conclusion: The tenant deposited rent with reasonable punctuality and therefore paid it regularly; exact or mathematical punctuality was not required. The eviction decree was set aside and the suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 12(3)(a) and 12(3)(b) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, clause (a) does not apply where the amount of standard rent is disputed. Under clause (b), a tenant who pays or deposits the rent and permitted increases then due by the first hearing or another date fixed by the court, thereafter pays or deposits them regularly until the suit is decided, and pays costs as directed, cannot be evicted for non-payment. Following Mranalini B. Shah v. Bapalal Mohanlal Shah, [1980] 4 SCC 251, regularity requires reasonable punctuality and substantial proximity to the due times, not clock-like precision; persistent payment at irregular intervals may fail the requirement.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_for_nonpayment and disputed_rent_amount and initial_arrears_paid_on_time and later_rent_payments_reasonably_punctual

predicates.rent_control_eviction_for_nonpayment: A landlord brought a rent-control proceeding seeking eviction on the ground of non-payment of rent.
predicates.disputed_rent_amount: The tenant and landlord disputed the amount of rent payable.
predicates.initial_arrears_paid_on_time: The tenant paid or deposited the rent arrears by the deadline fixed by the court.
predicates.later_rent_payments_reasonably_punctual: After paying the initial arrears, the tenant made later payments close to the required times, with only limited delays and most rent paid in advance.

issues.definition: When a rent-control eviction proceeding concerns non-payment, the rent amount is disputed, the initial arrears are paid on time, and later payments are reasonably punctual, an eviction decree for non-payment is barred.
